claim: Human skeletal muscle organoids can be differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cell lines.
source: Here we report that human skeletal muscle organoids can be differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cell lines to contain paraxial mesoderm and neuromesodermal progenitors and develop into organized structures reassembling neural plate border and dermomyotome.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Skeletal muscle organoids contain paraxial mesoderm and neuromesodermal progenitors.
source: Here we report that human skeletal muscle organoids can be differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cell lines to contain paraxial mesoderm and neuromesodermal progenitors and develop into organized structures reassembling neural plate border and dermomyotome.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the organoids contain these progenitor types, supported by experimental data.

claim: Skeletal muscle organoids develop into organized structures resembling neural plate border and dermomyotome.
source: Here we report that human skeletal muscle organoids can be differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cell lines to contain paraxial mesoderm and neuromesodermal progenitors and develop into organized structures reassembling neural plate border and dermomyotome.
evidence: This structural development is explicitly described in the abstract and supported by experimental observations.

claim: Culture conditions instigate neural lineage arrest in skeletal muscle organoids.
source: Culture conditions instigate neural lineage arrest and promote fetal hypaxial myogenesis toward limb axial anatomical identity, with generation of sustainable uncommitted PAX7 myogenic progenitors and fibroadipogenic (PDGFRa+) progenitor populations equivalent to those from the second trimester of human gestation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that culture conditions cause neural lineage arrest, supported by experimental data.

claim: Culture conditions promote fetal hypaxial myogenesis toward limb axial anatomical identity.
source: Culture conditions instigate neural lineage arrest and promote fetal hypaxial myogenesis toward limb axial anatomical identity, with generation of sustainable uncommitted PAX7 myogenic progenitors and fibroadipogenic (PDGFRa+) progenitor populations equivalent to those from the second trimester of human gestation.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract as a finding from the experimental protocol.

claim: Skeletal muscle organoids generate sustainable uncommitted PAX7 myogenic progenitors.
source: Culture conditions instigate neural lineage arrest and promote fetal hypaxial myogenesis toward limb axial anatomical identity, with generation of sustainable uncommitted PAX7 myogenic progenitors and fibroadipogenic (PDGFRa+) progenitor populations equivalent to those from the second trimester of human gestation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the generation of PAX7 myogenic progenitors, supported by experimental data.

claim: Skeletal muscle organoids generate fibroadipogenic (PDGFRa+) progenitor populations.
source: Culture conditions instigate neural lineage arrest and promote fetal hypaxial myogenesis toward limb axial anatomical identity, with generation of sustainable uncommitted PAX7 myogenic progenitors and fibroadipogenic (PDGFRa+) progenitor populations equivalent to those from the second trimester of human gestation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly mentions the generation of PDGFRa+ progenitor populations.

claim: Organoid-derived progenitor populations are equivalent to those from the second trimester of human gestation.
source: Culture conditions instigate neural lineage arrest and promote fetal hypaxial myogenesis toward limb axial anatomical identity, with generation of sustainable uncommitted PAX7 myogenic progenitors and fibroadipogenic (PDGFRa+) progenitor populations equivalent to those from the second trimester of human gestation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states equivalence to second trimester human gestation, supported by comparative analysis.

claim: Single-cell comparison reveals distinct molecular signatures for non-dividing myogenic progenitors in activated state characterized by CD44High/CD98+/MYOD1+ expression.
source: Single-cell comparison to human fetal and adult myogenic progenitor /satellite cells reveals distinct molecular signatures for non-dividing myogenic progenitors in activated (CD44High/CD98+/MYOD1+) and dormant (PAX7High/FBN1High/SPRY1High) states.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes molecular signatures identified through single-cell analysis.

claim: Single-cell comparison reveals distinct molecular signatures for non-dividing myogenic progenitors in dormant state characterized by PAX7High/FBN1High/SPRY1High expression.
source: Single-cell comparison to human fetal and adult myogenic progenitor /satellite cells reveals distinct molecular signatures for non-dividing myogenic progenitors in activated (CD44High/CD98+/MYOD1+) and dormant (PAX7High/FBN1High/SPRY1High) states.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes molecular signatures for dormant state identified through single-cell analysis.

claim: In vitro culture systems that structurally model human myogenesis have not been established.
source: In vitro culture systems that structurally model human myogenesis and promote PAX7+ myogenic progenitor maturation have not been established.
evidence: This is stated as background context in the abstract, representing a gap in the field.

claim: In vitro culture systems that promote PAX7+ myogenic progenitor maturation have not been established.
source: In vitro culture systems that structurally model human myogenesis and promote PAX7+ myogenic progenitor maturation have not been established.
evidence: This is stated as background context in the abstract, representing a gap in the field.

claim: Novel skeletal muscle model systems are required to further elucidate the process of human myogenesis.
source: Novel skeletal muscle model systems are required to further elucidate the process of human myogenesis as well as investigate muscular disorders and potential gene, cell, or drug therapies.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as motivation for the research.

claim: Novel skeletal muscle model systems are required to investigate muscular disorders and potential therapies.
source: Novel skeletal muscle model systems are required to further elucidate the process of human myogenesis as well as investigate muscular disorders and potential gene, cell, or drug therapies.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as motivation for the research.

claim: Two-dimensional culture conditions guide pluripotent stem cell differentiation toward skeletal muscle lineage using sequential growth factor applications.
source: Two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions guide pluripotent stem cell (PSC) differentiation toward skeletal muscle lineage using sequential growth factor applications and/or conditional PAX7 expression (Chal et al., 2015; Xi et al., 2017; Shelton et al., 2014; Borchin et al., 2013; Darabi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as background information with supporting citations.

claim: Two-dimensional culture conditions guide pluripotent stem cell differentiation toward skeletal muscle lineage using conditional PAX7 expression.
source: Two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions guide pluripotent stem cell (PSC) differentiation toward skeletal muscle lineage using sequential growth factor applications and/or conditional PAX7 expression (Chal et al., 2015; Xi et al., 2017; Shelton et al., 2014; Borchin et al., 2013; Darabi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as background information with supporting citations.

claim: Surface marker expression can be utilized to isolate myogenic progenitors with in vivo repopulation potential.
source: Further, surface marker expression can be utilized to isolate myogenic progenitors with in vivo repopulation potential (Magli et al., 2017; Hicks et al., 2018; Al Tanoury et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as background information with supporting citations.

claim: Three-dimensional differentiation approaches have provided cohorts of terminally differentiated myofibers.
source: While the few described three-dimensional (3D) differentiation approaches have provided cohorts of terminally differentiated myofibers, focus on potential interactions with the vasculature and nervous system has neglected assessment of the developmental identity or sustainability of myogenic progenitors (Faustino Martins et al., 2020; Maffioletti et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as background information with supporting citations.

claim: Three-dimensional differentiation approaches have neglected assessment of the developmental identity of myogenic progenitors.
source: While the few described three-dimensional (3D) differentiation approaches have provided cohorts of terminally differentiated myofibers, focus on potential interactions with the vasculature and nervous system has neglected assessment of the developmental identity or sustainability of myogenic progenitors (Faustino Martins et al., 2020; Maffioletti et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a critique of existing approaches with supporting citations.

claim: Three-dimensional differentiation approaches have neglected assessment of the sustainability of myogenic progenitors.
source: While the few described three-dimensional (3D) differentiation approaches have provided cohorts of terminally differentiated myofibers, focus on potential interactions with the vasculature and nervous system has neglected assessment of the developmental identity or sustainability of myogenic progenitors (Faustino Martins et al., 2020; Maffioletti et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a critique of existing approaches with supporting citations.

claim: Single-cell technologies provide databases for deciphering myogenic trajectories and expression profiles.
source: Single-cell technologies increasingly provide databases for deciphering myogenic trajectories and expression profiles of myogenic stem and progenitor cells (Barruet et al., 2020; Rubenstein et al., 2020; Xi et al., 2020), enabling full evaluation of the ability of PSC differentiation protocols to mimic human development.
evidence: This is stated as background information with supporting citations.

claim: Translation to model muscular dystrophies necessitates methods that provide expandable populations of muscle progenitors while promoting self-renewal and preserving a quiescent state.
source: Translation to model muscular dystrophies and investigate potential interventions in vitro necessitates methods that provide expandable populations of muscle progenitors while promoting self-renewal and preserving a quiescent, non-dividing, state (Quarta et al., 2016; Montarras et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for translational applications with supporting citations.

claim: Most vertebrate skeletal muscle progenitors develop from the paraxial mesoderm via transient embryonic developmental structures.
source: Most vertebrate skeletal muscle progenitors develop from the paraxial mesoderm via transient embryonic developmental structures (somites and dermomyotome) into the skeletal muscle system that spans the whole body.
evidence: This is stated as established biological knowledge.

claim: Stimulation with CHIR99021, LDN193189, and bFGF promoted paraxial mesoderm formation through derivation of BRACHYURY+ and TBX6+ cells.
source: Upon Matrigel embedding, stimulation with CHIR99021, LDN193189, and bFGF promoted paraxial mesoderm formation through derivation of BRACHYURY+ and TBX6+ cells (Figure 1A and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by figure references showing experimental data.

claim: Immunostaining on day 5 depicted the presence of mesodermal (BRACHYURY+), paraxial mesodermal (TBX6+), and neuromesodermal (SOX2+/BRACHYURY+) progenitors.
source: Immunostaining on day 5 depicted the presence of mesodermal (BRACHYURY+), paraxial mesodermal (TBX6+), and neuromesodermal (SOX2+/BRACHYURY+) progenitors (Gouti et al., 2017; Henrique et al., 2015; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference and supporting citations.

claim: Distinct PAX3+ but SOX2- cells emerged on the organoid surface on day 7.
source: Consequently, distinct PAX3+ but SOX2- cells emerged on the organoid surface (Figure 1D), followed by a significant downregulation of PSM markers HES7, TBX6, and MSGN1 (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing experimental observations.

claim: There was significant downregulation of PSM markers HES7, TBX6, and MSGN1 following day 7.
source: Consequently, distinct PAX3+ but SOX2- cells emerged on the organoid surface (Figure 1D), followed by a significant downregulation of PSM markers HES7, TBX6, and MSGN1 (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing experimental data.

claim: There was significant upregulation of ASM marker MEOX2 and neural crest marker TFAP2A.
source: Concomitantly, we observed significant upregulation of ASM marker MEOX2 and neural crest marker TFAP2A but not of SOX2 or PAX6, excluding a shift toward neural tube formation (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing experimental data.

claim: The absence of SOX2 or PAX6 upregulation excludes a shift toward neural tube formation.
source: Concomitantly, we observed significant upregulation of ASM marker MEOX2 and neural crest marker TFAP2A but not of SOX2 or PAX6, excluding a shift toward neural tube formation (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Dermomyotomal fate was promoted by Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) and WNT1A stimulation.
source: Dermomyotomal fate was promoted by Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) and WNT1A stimulation, while maintaining BMP inhibition avoided lateral mesoderm formation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing the protocol.

claim: Maintaining BMP inhibition avoided lateral mesoderm formation.
source: Dermomyotomal fate was promoted by Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) and WNT1A stimulation, while maintaining BMP inhibition avoided lateral mesoderm formation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing the protocol.

claim: Expression profiling on day 11 depicted presence of neural tube/crest (SOX2, PAX6, TFAP2A, SOX10 upregulation) and mesodermal (UNCX, TBX18, PAX3) lineages.
source: Expression profiling on day 11 depicted presence of neural tube/crest (SOX2, PAX6, TFAP2A, SOX10 upregulation) and mesodermal (UNCX, TBX18, PAX3) lineages and further downregulation of PSM markers (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing expression profiling data.

claim: The dermomyotomal/neural crest marker PAX7 emerged together with markers that define the dorsomedial (EN1) or ventrolateral portion (SIM1) of the dermomyotome.
source: Notably, the dermomyotomal/neural crest marker PAX7 emerged together with markers that define the dorsomedial (EN1) or ventrolateral portion (SIM1) of the dermomyotome (Cheng et al., 2004; Figure 1D and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citation.

claim: Organoids constituted a mosaic of neural crest and myogenic progenitor cells on day 17.
source: Surprisingly, on day 17, organoids constituted a mosaic of neural crest and myogenic progenitor cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: Cells with epithelial morphology were TFAP2A+, SOX2+, PAX3+, and PAX7+, indicating formation of neural plate border epithelium.
source: Cells with epithelial morphology were TFAP2A+, SOX2+, PAX3+, and PAX7+, indicating formation of neural plate border epithelium (Roellig et al., 2017; Figure 1G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference and supporting citation.

claim: In cell clusters with mesenchymal morphology, specified migrating PAX3+/SOX10+ neural crest progenitors and PAX3+/SOX2-/SOX10- cells of myogenic origin were detected.
source: In cell clusters with mesenchymal morphology, we detected specified migrating PAX3+/SOX10+ neural crest progenitors and PAX3+/SOX2-/SOX10- cells of myogenic origin (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing experimental observations.

claim: Myogenic lineages on day 17 appeared to be primarily represented by PAX3+ (9.35 ± 0.07%) rather than PAX7+ cells.
source: At this stage, myogenic lineages appeared to be primarily represented by PAX3+ (9.35 ± 0.07%) rather than PAX7+ cells, as the PAX7 expression pattern (15.3 ± 0.1% PAX3+/PAX7+, 5.11 ± 0.13% PAX7+) predominantly overlapped with that of SOX2 and TFAP2A (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with quantitative data and figure references.

claim: Omitting FGF stimulation from day 17 onward ceased neural crest development and promoted delamination/migration of PAX3+/PAX7+/SOX10- progenitor cells.
source: From day 17 onward, we omitted FGF stimulation to cease neural crest development and promote delamination/migration of PAX3+/PAX7+/SOX10- progenitor cells (Murphy et al., 1994; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference and supporting citation.

claim: Committed myogenic populations were observed through detection of fast MyHC myofibers in the proximity of PAX7+ but SOX2-/TFAP2A-/SOX10- negative cells by day 23.
source: Strikingly, until day 23, we observed committed myogenic populations through detection of fast MyHC myofibers in the proximity of PAX7+ but SOX2-/TFAP2A-/SOX10- negative cells (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing experimental observations.

claim: Expression profiling indicated downregulation of neural tube/crest lineage markers and significant upregulation of muscle precursor migrating markers such as LBX1, CXCR4, and MEOX2.
source: Consistently, expression profiling indicated downregulation of neural tube/crest lineage markers and significant upregulation of muscle precursor migrating markers (Buckingham and Rigby, 2014), such as LBX1, CXCR4, and MEOX2 (1,2Figures 1E and 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A ).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citation.

claim: At 8 weeks, organoids showed profound changes in transcription profiling.
source: At 8 wk, organoids showed profound changes in transcription profiling (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing transcriptional data.

claim: Gene ontology enrichment analysis highlighted muscle development, muscle contraction, and myofibril assembly among the top upregulated gene ontology terms at 8 weeks.
source: Gene ontology enrichment analysis highlighted an ongoing developmental transition with muscle development, muscle contraction, and myofibril assembly among the top upregulated gene ontology terms and neurogenesis and nervous system development among the top downregulated terms (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing gene ontology analysis.

claim: Gene ontology enrichment analysis highlighted neurogenesis and nervous system development among the top downregulated terms at 8 weeks.
source: Gene ontology enrichment analysis highlighted an ongoing developmental transition with muscle development, muscle contraction, and myofibril assembly among the top upregulated gene ontology terms and neurogenesis and nervous system development among the top downregulated terms (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing gene ontology analysis.

claim: Downregulation of key markers characterizing neural tube and neural crest development was detected, such as PAK3, DLX5, B3GAT1, FOXB1, HES5, and OLIG3.
source: In addition, we detected downregulation of key markers characterizing neural tube and neural crest development (Soldatov et al., 2019), such as PAK3, DLX5, B3GAT1, FOXB1, HES5, and OLIG3 (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citation.

claim: SOX2, TFAP2A, and SOX10-expressing cells were restricted to the inner portion of the organoid at 5 weeks.
source: Interestingly, we could spatially visualize this process using immunocytochemistry for SOX2, TFAP2A, and SOX10-expressing cells that were restricted to the inner portion of the organoid, and probably not susceptible to culture stimulation at 5 wk (1,2Figures 1H, 2C and D , Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing spatial distribution.

claim: TUJ1+ neurons were confined to inner organoid areas and close to SOX2+ epithelium on day 84, while FastMyHC+ myofibers occupied exterior areas.
source: This neural/myogenic lineage spatial orientation could be visualized even on day 84 through the presence of TUJ1+ neurons confined to inner organoid areas and close to SOX2+ epithelium, while FastMyHC+ myofibers occupied exterior areas (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing spatial organization.

claim: Substantial proportions of migratory cells in proximity of FastMyHC+, MF20+ myofibers expressed PAX7 (40 ± 0.3%) but not SOX2, TFAP2A, SOX10, or MYOD1 (3.55 ± 0.32%).
source: On the other hand, substantial proportions of migratory cells in proximity of FastMyHC+, MF20+ myofibers expressed PAX7 (40 ± 0.3%) but not SOX2, TFAP2A, SOX10, or MYOD1 (3.55 ± 0.32%) (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with quantitative data and figure references.

claim: Culture progression led to a significant increase in PAX7+ and MYOD1+ cells at 8 weeks (45.3 ± 3.4% and 49.8 ± 0.62%, respectively).
source: Culture progression led to a significant increase in PAX7+ and MYOD1+ cells at 8 wk (45.3 ± 3,4% and 49.8 ± 0.62%, respectively) (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), suggesting an interval in which organoid culture predominantly commits to myogenic lineage.
evidence: This is explicitly stated with quantitative data and figure references.

claim: Expression profiling at 8 weeks depicted upregulation of markers characteristic for limb migrating myogenic cells, for example, LBX1, PAX7, SIX1/4, EYA1/4, PITX2, MYF5, TCF4, and MSX1.
source: Expression profiling at this stage depicted upregulation of markers characteristic for limb migrating myogenic cells, for example, LBX1, PAX7, SIX1/4, EYA1/4, PITX2, MYF5, TCF4, and MSX1 (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing expression profiling data.

claim: HOX gene cluster profiling at 4 weeks correlated HOX A9, B9, C9 upregulation with limb bud site.
source: Consequently, HOX gene cluster profiling at 4 wk correlated HOX A9, B9, C9 upregulation with limb bud site, while upregulation of the HOX 10–13 cluster during 8–16 wk attributed later organoid development to a more distal limb axial anatomical identity (Shubin et al., 1997; Xu and Wellik, 2011; Raines et al., 2015; Figure 2G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference and supporting citations.

claim: Upregulation of the HOX 10–13 cluster during 8–16 weeks attributed later organoid development to a more distal limb axial anatomical identity.
source: Consequently, HOX gene cluster profiling at 4 wk correlated HOX A9, B9, C9 upregulation with limb bud site, while upregulation of the HOX 10–13 cluster during 8–16 wk attributed later organoid development to a more distal limb axial anatomical identity (Shubin et al., 1997; Xu and Wellik, 2011; Raines et al., 2015; Figure 2G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference and supporting citations.

claim: Analysis of organoid culture at single-cell resolution indicated predominant presence of skeletal muscle lineage (n = 3945 cells, 91.26% of total population).
source: Analysis of organoid culture at single-cell resolution indicated predominant presence of skeletal muscle lineage (n = 3945 cells, 91.26% of total population), complemented with two smaller cell clusters of mesenchymal/'fibroadipogenic' (n = 165 cells, 3.82% of total population), and neural (n = 213 cells, 4.93% of total population) origin (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with quantitative data and figure references.

claim: Skeletal muscle lineages separated into distinct subclusters: myogenic muscle progenitors in non-dividing (PAX7+/PAX3-) and mitotic states (PAX7+/CDK1+/KI67+), myoblasts (MYOD1+), myocytes (MYOG+), and myotubes (MYH3+).
source: Skeletal muscle lineages further separated into distinct subclusters: myogenic muscle progenitors in non-dividing (PAX7+/PAX3-) and mitotic states (PAX7+/CDK1+/KI67+), myoblasts (MYOD1+), myocytes (MYOG+), and myotubes (MYH3+) (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing single-cell clustering.

claim: A distinct cell population with PDGFRa among the top upregulated genes suggested fibroadipogenic potential.
source: Further, investigation of mesenchymal cluster identity suggested fibroadipogenic potential of a distinct cell population with PDGFRa among the top upregulated genes (Uezumi et al., 2010; Uezumi et al., 2011; Xi et al., 2020; Figure 3A and F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citations.

claim: Adipogenic potential was highlighted through upregulation of PREF-1 and EBF2.
source: Moreover, adipogenic potential was highlighted through upregulation of PREF-1 and EBF2 (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing gene expression.

claim: Structures resembling adipocytes were detected from 9–10 weeks onward, with adipogenic nature verified by PRDM16 and Oil red O positive staining.
source: Occasionally, we detected structures resembling adipocytes from 9–10 wk onward, with adipogenic nature verified by PRDM16 and Oil red O positive staining (Figure 3B and D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing staining results.

claim: Myogenesis progression based on t-SNE feature and Violin plots indicated gradual transitions from myogenic progenitor to myotube subclusters.
source: Myogenesis progression based on t-SNE feature and Violin plots of key markers from each stage indicated gradual transitions from myogenic progenitor to myotube subclusters (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing trajectory analysis.

claim: MyHC expression profiling at single-cell resolution demonstrated predominant presence of embryonic (MYH3+) and perinatal (MYH8+) myofibers.
source: MyHC expression profiling at single-cell resolution demonstrated predominant presence of embryonic (MYH3+) and perinatal (MYH8+) myofibers, co-expressing β-Enolase and M-cadherin in the vicinity of PAX7+ cells (Figure 3G–J).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing expression profiling.

claim: At more mature stages, adult MYH1 or slow MYH7 isoforms were detected.
source: At more mature stages, we detected adult MYH1 or slow MYH7 isoforms (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G), presumably due to myofiber stimulation via spontaneous contraction.
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference and speculation about mechanism.

claim: Differential expression comparison between 8 and 16 week organoids indicated less variance in transcription profiling.
source: In agreement, differential expression comparison between 8 and 16 wk organoids indicated less variance in transcription profiling (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1H, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing comparative analysis.

claim: Sarcomere organization, ion transport, response to stimulus, and synapse structure maintenance were among the upregulated gene ontology terms between 8 and 16 weeks.
source: Consistently, sarcomere organization, ion transport, response to stimulus, and synapse structure maintenance were among the upregulated gene ontology terms and mitosis, cell cycle, DNA packaging, and nuclear division among the top downregulated terms (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing gene ontology analysis.

claim: Mitosis, cell cycle, DNA packaging, and nuclear division were among the top downregulated terms between 8 and 16 weeks.
source: Consistently, sarcomere organization, ion transport, response to stimulus, and synapse structure maintenance were among the upregulated gene ontology terms and mitosis, cell cycle, DNA packaging, and nuclear division among the top downregulated terms (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing gene ontology analysis.

claim: At 14 weeks, significant increases in PAX7+ (50.16 ± 2.19%) and MYOD1+ (58.53 ± 0.92%) cells were reported.
source: Notably, ongoing maturation did not affect pool of progenitor cells, as even at 14 wk we could report significant increases in PAX7+ (50,16 ± 2.19%) and MYOD1+ (58.53 ± 0.92%) cells (2,3Figures 2F and 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and F).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with quantitative data and figure references.

claim: Immunocytochemistry revealed positive staining for dystrophin and a continuous laminin sheath around individual muscle fibers.
source: Regarding localization and functionality of organoid-derived myofibers, immunocytochemistry revealed positive staining for dystrophin and a continuous laminin sheath around individual muscle fibers.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observation from immunocytochemistry.

claim: Ultrastructure and two-photon microscopy analysis depicted well-developed sarcomeres.
source: Ultrastructure and two-photon microscopy analysis depicted well-developed sarcomeres (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing microscopy data.

claim: Patch-clamp experiments upon superfusion of cells with acetylcholine indicated inward current generations that rapidly declined to a low steady-state level.
source: Moreover, patch-clamp experiments, upon superfusion of cells with acetylcholine (ACh), indicated inward current generations that rapidly declined to a low steady-state level (Figure 3K, Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing electrophysiology data.

claim: The I/V curve of the acetylcholine-induced current component showed almost linear behavior and reversal potential around 0 mV.
source: The I/V curve of this current component showed almost linear behavior and reversal potential around 0 mV (Figure 3L).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure reference showing electrophysiology data.

claim: Application of a fluorescent biosensor for monitoring changes in cytosolic Ca2+ (Twitch2B) revealed nAChR efficiency in modulating intracellular [Ca2+].
source: Application of a fluorescent biosensor for monitoring changes in cytosolic Ca2+ (Twitch2B) revealed nAChR efficiency in modulating intracellular [Ca2+].
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from the biosensor experiments.

claim: Fetal muscle progenitors and electrophysiologically functional myofibers were successfully derived from hiPSC lines with wild type and Duchenne muscular dystrophy genetic backgrounds.
source: Using our organoid protocol, we successfully derived fetal muscle progenitors and electrophysiologically functional myofibers from hiPSC lines with wild type and Duchenne muscular dystrophy genetic backgrounds (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing data from different cell lines.

claim: Initial screening of PAX7+ progenitors indicated expression of several satellite cell markers such as CD82, CAV1, FGFR1, FGFR4, EGFR, M-Cadherin, NCAM, FZD7, CXCR4, ITGβ1, ITGA7, SCD2, and SCD4.
source: Initial screening of PAX7+ progenitors indicated expression of several satellite cell markers (Fukada et al., 2007), such as CD82, CAV1, FGFR1, FGFR4, EGFR, M-Cadherin, NCAM, FZD7, CXCR4, ITGβ1, ITGA7, SCD2, and SCD4 (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citation.

claim: Further investigation verified NOTCH signaling activity (HES1, HEYL, HEY1, and NRARP) in the myogenic subcluster.
source: Further investigation verified NOTCH signaling activity (HES1, HEYL, HEY1, and NRARP) in the myogenic subcluster, while dormant myogenic progenitors exhibited high expression of SPRY1 and cell cycle inhibitors p57 (CDKN1C), p21, and PMP22 (Xi et al., 2020; Fukada et al., 2007; Bjornson et al., 2012; Shea et al., 2010; Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citations.

claim: Dormant myogenic progenitors exhibited high expression of SPRY1 and cell cycle inhibitors p57 (CDKN1C), p21, and PMP22.
source: Further investigation verified NOTCH signaling activity (HES1, HEYL, HEY1, and NRARP) in the myogenic subcluster, while dormant myogenic progenitors exhibited high expression of SPRY1 and cell cycle inhibitors p57 (CDKN1C), p21, and PMP22 (Xi et al., 2020; Fukada et al., 2007; Bjornson et al., 2012; Shea et al., 2010; Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references and supporting citations.

claim: Proliferation assays performed at 14 weeks demonstrated 4.78 ± 0.28% EdU+ cells.
source: Moreover, proliferation assays performed at the same stage (14 wk) demonstrated 4.78 ± 0.28% edU+ cells, while substantial proportions of PAX7+ myogenic progenitors remained quiescent (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with quantitative data and figure references.

claim: Substantial proportions of PAX7+ myogenic progenitors remained quiescent at 14 weeks.
source: Moreover, proliferation assays performed at the same stage (14 wk) demonstrated 4.78 ± 0.28% edU+ cells, while substantial proportions of PAX7+ myogenic progenitors remained quiescent (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing proliferation data.

claim: t-SNE clustering divided myogenic progenitors into three distinct groups with unique molecular signatures: 'CD44high,' 'FBN1high,' and 'CDK1+' clusters.
source: t-SNE clustering divided myogenic progenitors into three distinct groups with unique molecular signatures: 'CD44high,' 'FBN1high,' and 'CDK1+' clusters (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with figure references showing clustering analysis.

claim: The 'CD44high' cluster, further characterized by CD98 upregulation, adopted a molecular signature similar to activated satellite cell state.
